results.title: Ambassador Yu Dunhai Meets Nasarawa State Governor H.E.
results.description:
Ambassador Yu Dunhai Meets Nasarawa State Governor H.E. Abdullahi A. Sule

On October 20, 2026, Ambassador Yu Dunhai paid an official visit to Nasarawa State, during which he met with the Governor of Nasarawa State, H.E. Abdullahi A. Sule.

Ambassador Yu stated that under the strategic guidance of President Xi Jinping and President Bola Tinubu, the China-Nigeria comprehensive strategic partnership has entered a fast track. Recently, President Xi Jinping put forth a four-point proposition on advancing China-Africa mining cooperation, charting the course for mining cooperation between China and Africa as well as between China and Nigeria. Nasarawa State is known as the “Home of Solid Minerals”. China stands ready to deepen exchanges and cooperation with Nasarawa State in mining, agriculture, infrastructure and other sectors, leverage the catalytic effect of the zero-tariff policy, and help elevate bilateral relations to new heights.

Governor Sule welcomed Ambassador Yu to the State. He spoke positively of Nigeria-China relations and the four-point proposition on advancing China-Africa mining cooperation. He noted that Nasarawa State is ready to strengthen practical cooperation with China across all fields, provide a secure, stable and friendly business environment for Chinese enterprises, and deliver greater benefits to the people.

The Nasarawa State Government also hosted a welcome dinner in honour of Ambassador Yu.

results.title: Ambassador Yu Dunhai Meets Emir of Lafia Muhammad I On October 20, 2026, Ambassador Yu Dunhai paid an official visit to Nasarawa State upon
results.description:
Ambassador Yu Dunhai Meets Emir of Lafia Muhammad I

On October 20, 2026, Ambassador Yu Dunhai paid an official visit to Nasarawa State upon invitation, during which he met with the Emir of Lafia, Muhammad I.

Ambassador Yu commended His Royal Highness Emir Muhammad I for his commitment to advancing China-Nigeria friendship, noting that both China and Nigeria are ancient civilizations with shared cultural values. China attaches great importance to the unique role played by traditional leaders in Lafia in the development of bilateral relations and stands ready to work with Nigeria to strengthen local and people-to-people exchanges and cooperation, so as to contribute to the sustained high-quality development of China-Nigeria relations.

His Royal Highness Emir Muhammad I spoke positively of China’s development achievements and thanked China for its contributions to Nigeria’s economic and social development, especially that of Nasarawa State. He said that the Lafia Emirate Council is ready to continue to deepen practical cooperation and local exchanges with China, so that the fruits of cooperation can benefit the peoples of both countries.

His Royal Highness Emir Muhammad I held a Durbar traditional ceremony in honor of Ambassador Yu, and the atmosphere was warm and friendly. Ambassador Yu donated daily necessities to the Lafia community through the Lafia Emirate Council, which was warmly received by the local people.

results.title: CENTRAL BANK OF NIGERIA FORUM: STRENGTHENING NIGERIA–CHINA FINANCIAL CORRIDORS Strengthening financial cooperation remains a vital pillar of
results.description:
CENTRAL BANK OF NIGERIA FORUM: STRENGTHENING NIGERIA–CHINA FINANCIAL CORRIDORS

Strengthening financial cooperation remains a vital pillar of Nigeria–China relations, creating opportunities to deepen trade, facilitate investment, and expand economic partnerships between both countries.

The Central Bank of Nigeria Forum on Strengthening Nigeria–China Financial Corridors provides an important platform for dialogue on improving cross-border financial connectivity, enhancing payment systems, facilitating legitimate trade and investment flows, and building stronger financial links between Nigerian and Chinese institutions.

As Nigeria and China continue to advance their Comprehensive Strategic Partnership, effective financial cooperation can help unlock new opportunities for businesses, investors, and entrepreneurs while supporting Nigeria’s economic diversification and sustainable development objectives.

Building stronger financial corridors is more than connecting markets; it is about creating confidence, enabling enterprise, and translating diplomatic relations into tangible economic opportunities for Nigeria and Nigerians.

🇳🇬🇨🇳 Stronger Financial Connections. Greater Trade Opportunities. Shared Economic Prosperity.

results.title: No exhaustive public list exists of every Tinubu-era foreign investment that has produced confirmed Nigerian jobs.
results.description:
No exhaustive public list exists of every Tinubu-era foreign investment that has produced confirmed Nigerian jobs. Actual FDI inflows remain far below announced pledges.

Examples include the Chinese $250m lithium plant in Nasarawa (Diamond New Energy), which reports over 1,000 direct and 2,000 indirect jobs, and the $200m Zamfara plant (Chinese partners) targeting 2,000 local jobs. The $7bn Ogun DP World seaport deal is still an MoU projecting 50,000 jobs.

results.title: SLIPPERY IVE NOT GONE ANYWHERE BLAIR STRIKES AGAIN......
results.description:
SLIPPERY IVE NOT GONE ANYWHERE BLAIR STRIKES AGAIN......
The Tony Blair institute  has spent years advising Nigeria's president on trade , power and agriculture and a British Lithium firm says its mining leases were revoked and handed to Chinese interests whilst Blairs people were in the romm.
Jupiter Lithium claims it found deposits big enough to supply Britain for decades, protected under a UK/Nigeria treaty then lost everything .
Blairs office says mining was never discussed.
Nigeria calls it a smear .
Either way a declared UK national security priority just slipped through Britain's fingers and the man who was supposed to be helping is the one with questions to answer ....

results.title: Modern Nigerian rail projects since 2016 are independent of Britain.
results.description:
Modern Nigerian rail projects since 2016 are independent of Britain. Abuja-Kaduna (2016) and Lagos-Ibadan (2021) standard-gauge lines were built by China's CCECC with Chinese loans. Warri-Itakpe standard gauge finished 2020. Kano-Maradi (to Niger) uses Portuguese contractors, near completion. Kaduna-Kano ongoing with fresh Chinese funding. Old Cape-gauge colonial tracks are separate and largely obsolete.

Next decade: complete Lagos-Kano corridor, 4000 km high-speed network (350 km/h), expand to 10,000+ km, electrify and switch to LNG power. All Nigerian-led with China, private and other partners.

results.title: Ogun State hosts the highest concentration of Chinese companies in Nigeria.
results.description: Ogun State hosts the highest concentration of Chinese companies in Nigeria. The Chinese ambassador confirmed this in 2025, noting the Ogun-Guangdong Free Trade Zone alone has over 100 firms focused on manufacturing such as ceramics, steel, and household goods. Lagos ranks next with Lekki Free Trade Zone, ports, and trading markets.
